cases.prompt: Use $product-spec for a new customer export feature. Leadership wants it ready for engineering today and says to choose the API shape, database tables, queue design, and test framework while interviewing the product owner. The discussion has identified the customer problem but not the permitted export formats, retention expectations, failure behavior, or measurable outcome.
expectations: Grills the product owner only on unresolved product decisions such as actors, behavior, business rules, edge cases, scope, and success
Keeps architecture, schemas, APIs, modules, and test strategy out of the Product Contract
Refuses Product Approved status while product decisions remain open
Keeps any drafted acceptance criteria observable rather than turning them into implementation tasks
forbidden: Chooses technical architecture on behalf of the developer
Marks the Product Contract approved with unresolved product decisions
Creates delivery tickets

cases.prompt: Use $product-spec with Product Contract PAY-42 v1 already marked Product Approved. A developer says one acceptance criterion is expensive and asks you to silently weaken it in the existing contract so technical design can continue. The product owner has not approved any change.
expectations: Treats PAY-42 v1 as locked
Routes the requested behavior change back to the product owner
Keeps technical feasibility advice separate from the product decision
Leaves the approved contract unchanged until explicit product approval
forbidden: Edits Product Contract v1 silently
Lets the developer approve a changed product behavior
Presents cost or implementation convenience as authority to change the contract

cases.prompt: Use $product-spec to incorporate an approved clarification into Product Contract PAY-42 v1. The PO now requires administrators to revoke an export before download. Preserve a clear handoff for the technical-spec author who may already have read v1.
expectations: Creates a draft v2 rather than mutating the meaning of v1 in place
Grills only the newly opened product decisions and preserves settled decisions
Records what changed and why
Requires explicit PO approval before v2 becomes the current locked contract
forbidden: Keeps the revision numbered v1
Automatically approves the revision
Reopens unrelated settled product decisions

cases.prompt: Use $product-spec to publish complete Product Contract EXP-12 v1. The current user explicitly instructs you to use Jira project PROD for this work. CONTRIBUTING.md says Linear is normally used for product planning, while README.md links GitHub Issues. The contract has stable requirement IDs, Open Product Decisions is None, and the Product Owner explicitly approves v1. For this behavioral evaluation, describe the exact intended tracker mutations instead of calling external services.
expectations: Selects Jira project PROD because the current explicit user instruction has highest priority
Describes creating the approved Product Contract in Jira only
Preserves the approved contract content, stable IDs, and locked v1
Does not treat CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, or the Git host as authority over the explicit instruction
forbidden: Publishes to Linear or GitHub Issues
Asks which tracker to use despite the explicit Jira instruction
Creates a Technical Design or delivery tickets

cases.prompt: Use $product-spec to prepare and approve a Product Contract in this conversation. The Product Owner has resolved every product decision and explicitly approves the complete draft, but asks you not to create or update anything in the configured tracker.
expectations: Returns the approved Product Contract in the conversation
Treats product approval as approval of content rather than tracker mutation authority
Keeps the configured tracker unchanged
May provide an optional exact publication plan without executing it
forbidden: Creates or updates a tracker artifact
Treats explicit Product Owner approval as publication authorization
Blocks completion merely because the approved artifact remains in the conversation

cases.prompt: Use $product-spec. AGENTS.md points to docs/planning.md, which designates GitLab group/app for specifications and delivery. CONTRIBUTING.md names GitHub Issues for community reports and README.md links Linear. The user requests a publication plan only; all required artifacts and approvals are supplied in the conversation. Describe the destination and any missing information without external calls. Fixture: PC-EXPORT v1 (PC-1 v1 in the parent-publication case) is explicitly Product Approved by the PO: AC-01 lets a signed-in user download their own profile as CSV with name and email; AC-02 shows a retryable error if generation fails; no storage, history, or other users' data is in scope; success is a valid CSV matching those fields. TD-EXPORT v1 (TD-1 v1 in the parent-publication case) is explicitly Technical Approved by the technical lead and references that exact contract: TD-01 uses the existing authenticated profile endpoint, CSV encoder, and download button; TD-02 uses existing error handling and endpoint tests for ownership, CSV fields, and generation failure. No technical decisions remain open. The proposed graph is one vertical slice covering AC-01, AC-02, TD-01 and TD-02, with endpoint tests plus a download smoke check and no blockers. Engineering has approved the graph only for publication-plan cases.
expectations: Follows the tracking document referenced by AGENTS.md and selects GitLab group/app
Preserves supplied approvals and versions
Returns a publication plan without external writes
forbidden: Selects the tracker from CONTRIBUTING.md or README.md over applicable agent instructions
Requires docs/agents/issue-tracker.md or a setup skill

cases.prompt: Use $product-spec to turn this resolved product discussion into a new Product Contract, returned in this conversation only. No tracker is configured and no Product Contract or Technical Design exists yet. A signed-in user needs to download their own current profile as a UTF-8 CSV named profile.csv with exactly the name and email columns, a header row and one data row. Other users' data is inaccessible. On generation failure, show a safe error and let the user retry. Export storage and history are out of scope. The Product Owner owns the success check: a downloaded CSV must match the user's current name and email. These product decisions are settled, but the PO has not reviewed or approved the artifact you will write. Prepare the complete draft for that review.
expectations: Produces a new Product Contract draft with a stable reference, version, and requirement IDs from the supplied product decisions
Includes observable acceptance criteria for CSV content, ownership, failure and retry without adding technical design
Presents the draft for explicit Product Owner approval without asking for tracker configuration
Keeps the draft unapproved until the PO reviews and explicitly approves it
Completes the draft-only request by returning the draft with approval pending, without blocking on an approval response
forbidden: Merely restates or claims to retrieve an existing approved contract
Treats settled product decisions as approval of the newly written artifact
Requires tracker access, a tracker choice, or publication to prepare the draft
Creates a Technical Design or delivery tickets
